description: Review-candidate mechanism extensions derived from r5 judge/backlog evidence. These entries are offline lexicon candidates; they are not online regex routing rules and require same-identity recall evaluation before paper-facing use.

mechanisms.name: LDAP filter or distinguished-name injection through unescaped input
mechanisms.source_shape: attacker-controlled usernames, account names, directory attributes, filter fragments, distinguished names, or LDAP query parameters
mechanisms.sink_shape: LDAP search filters, distinguished-name construction, directory queries, or LDAP bind/search operations
mechanisms.missing_guard: LDAP metacharacters and distinguished-name syntax are not escaped or parameterized for the exact LDAP context before the query
mechanisms.typical_fix: use context-specific LDAP filter or DN escaping, parameterized filter construction where available, and allowlist structural query fragments

mechanisms.name: HTML sanitizer policy gap or inactive allowlist
mechanisms.source_shape: attacker-controlled markup, HTML fragments, rich text, comments, DOM nodes, style blocks, attributes, or URI values
mechanisms.sink_shape: HTML cleaners, SafeHtml validators, DOM sanitizers, rich-text renderers, or browser-rendered sanitized output
mechanisms.missing_guard: the active sanitizer policy does not allowlist dangerous elements, attributes, URI schemes, DOM child nodes, comments, or malformed inputs before rendering
mechanisms.typical_fix: activate the restrictive sanitizer for the relevant mode, enforce element/attribute/URI allowlists after parsing, and add regression tests for the bypass form

mechanisms.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanisms.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanisms.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanisms.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanisms.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

mechanisms.name: authentication artifact accepted without complete validation
mechanisms.source_shape: externally supplied authentication artifacts such as JWTs, SAML responses, OAuth authorization codes, bearer tokens, session cookies, or client credentials
mechanisms.sink_shape: session creation, identity binding, privilege assignment, protected API access, or credential exchange decisions
mechanisms.missing_guard: signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce, binding, proof-of-possession, or protocol state validation is incomplete before accepting the identity
mechanisms.typical_fix: validate all required cryptographic and protocol fields before creating a principal or granting access, and bind the artifact to the intended client, audience, and session

mechanisms.name: dynamic SQL query construction from untrusted fragments
mechanisms.source_shape: attacker-controlled request values, filters, identifiers, sort fields, expressions, or configuration values
mechanisms.sink_shape: SQL statement strings, JDBC Statement execution, query builders with raw fragments, or database filters
mechanisms.missing_guard: values or structural fragments are concatenated into SQL syntax without parameter binding or a strict allowlist for identifiers and operators
mechanisms.typical_fix: use bound parameters for values, allowlist structural SQL fragments, and keep untrusted data out of query syntax

mechanisms.name: browser-rendered file download through unsafe inline content disposition
mechanisms.source_shape: stored or user-uploaded file content, MIME metadata, filenames, or request parameters that choose inline versus attachment rendering
mechanisms.sink_shape: HTTP file-download responses, browser-rendered attachments, content-disposition headers, or content-type selection
mechanisms.missing_guard: browser-renderable content is served inline without an allowlist, forced attachment disposition, safe content type, or content sniffing protection
mechanisms.typical_fix: force attachment for untrusted content unless an allowlisted safe type is proven, set safe content types and nosniff headers, and separate trusted preview paths from raw downloads

mechanisms.name: temporary resource created with insecure permissions
mechanisms.source_shape: temporary files or directories created for sensitive data, build artifacts, credentials, extracted content, or intermediate processing
mechanisms.sink_shape: filesystem creation APIs that inherit broad default permissions or fail to apply owner-only permissions before use
mechanisms.missing_guard: the temporary resource is created or exposed with permissions that allow other local users to read, write, replace, or observe sensitive content
mechanisms.typical_fix: create temporary resources with owner-only permissions atomically, verify permission-setting success, and avoid placing secrets in shared-readable locations

mechanisms.name: archive extraction escape through symlink-following writes
mechanisms.source_shape: attacker-controlled archive entries, symlink entries, link targets, or extraction order
mechanisms.sink_shape: archive extraction code that creates links, opens output files, or writes entry contents into the extraction tree
mechanisms.missing_guard: later writes can follow an existing or archive-created symbolic link outside the extraction root despite lexical or canonical path containment checks
mechanisms.typical_fix: reject unsafe symlink targets, use no-follow or race-safe filesystem operations for writes, and validate the final opened target remains inside the extraction root
